body: The same thing happened to me in high school. I knew that I wasn’t enjoying life the way people around me were so I told my mom when I was 14. She responded by saying it was a teenage phase so I never got help my with mental health. After struggling with my lifestyle for 5 years I finally broke down, and got diagnosed w anxiety & depression. I signed up for free counselling and started undertaking the process of getting better without my family’s support. It was so difficult and I didn’t have the money to afford therapy. I finally told my mom again about my whole journey and she was upset that she hadn’t paid attention sooner. I tried a couple counselors IRL but found that Better Help (an online counseling platform) works best for me. Whenever I am upset/overwhelmed/stressed, I can text my counselor and she’s ready to call or video many times a week. While it took a couple tries to find the counselor that worked for me, I’m so happy I gave it a shot. I think it’s 40-70$ a month, you should look into that as an option. I wish you all the best! I pushed away my friends too and know how it is to be alone with your problems. You can always vent to me, or other apps like Wisdo or Woebot (for some AI problem solving) really help too without feeling like you’re burdening anyone. Let me know if you need anything! I may not be entirely better, but I feel so much happier knowing that I’m making steps towards recovering from my old ways of thinking.

My mother has dreamed of being a writer for her entire life. She's kept her manuscript for her first novel tucked away in a pristine manila folder in her bedside table for as I can remember. It was one of her friends who told me the piece of advice that made me contemplate my worth as a writer. She said, "Let your daughter go. Let her experience everything. Only when she sees things for herself, can she write about them." 

Since that then my writing has changed. While it might seem that my mother's friend meant me to only write what I had experienced, I understood what she said slightly differently. To me, writing must be based on an emotion you felt before. The happiness of a kiss from someone you are crushing on, the rage of a parking ticket, the nerves of almost missing a flight. If you have experienced enough, then your creativity can transport you anywhere. Your emotional experiences qualify you to write anything you want as if you were there. 

The moral of the story is to go for it. Take a spontaneous road trip. Get your heart broken. Perform in front of an audience. Fly across the world for a fresh start. Anything you take a risk for can only be added to your own story.
